title: Hardik Pandya May Not Return to Action Before IPL 2027
excerpt: Recovering from a shin stress injury at the BCCI Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru, the India all-rounder is expected to miss the New Zealand, Sri Lanka and Zimbabwe series, with IPL 2027 emerging as his likely comeback.
body:
• Hardik Pandya is recovering from a stress injury on the inner side of his shin at the BCCI Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru, and reports say he may not play competitive cricket again before IPL 2027.
  • Pandya is expected to start jogging in about three weeks, with his running load then increased gradually over eight weeks; no deadline has been set for full match fitness.
  • He has not been selected for the New Zealand tour and is expected to miss the Sri Lanka series starting December 13 and the Zimbabwe ODI series starting January 3.
  • Pandya last played in IPL 2026 for Mumbai Indians in May; his last international appearance was the T20 World Cup final in March 2026.

Pandya facing months more on the sidelines

India all-rounder Hardik Pandya may not return to competitive cricket before the Indian Premier League season in 2027, according to reports detailing the latest assessment of his shin stress injury. Pandya, 32, is undergoing rehabilitation at the Board of Control for Cricket in India's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru, and the medical team has not set a deadline for him to regain full match fitness. The reporting, first carried by Dainik Jagran journalist Abhishek Tripathi and summarised by CricketNews, says Pandya is recovering slowly from a stress injury on the inner part of his shin bone.

Pandya's medical reports were reviewed last week by Dr Dinshaw Pardiwala, according to The Daily Jagran. He is expected to start jogging after three weeks, after which his running workload will be increased gradually over the following eight weeks. His strength training is also being stepped up in stages under medical supervision, with the programme designed to avoid putting additional stress on the injured area.

A long list of missed series

Pandya has already missed a large part of India's 2026 calendar. He was unavailable for the home ODI series against Afghanistan, the tours of Ireland and England, the T20I series in Zimbabwe, a further T20I series against Afghanistan, the home white-ball series against the West Indies and the Asian Games 2026 in Japan. He was named in an India A squad for a home series against Australia A with his participation subject to fitness, but he did not recover in time for those games.

He has not been selected for the New Zealand tour. On the reported timeline, the Sri Lanka white-ball series starting December 13 and the Zimbabwe ODI series starting January 3 also fall too early. By the time he approaches match fitness, the domestic Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy and Vijay Hazare Trophy will have ended, removing the usual route back through domestic cricket. India then play the five-Test Border-Gavaskar Trophy against Australia from January 21 to March 3, a format Pandya no longer plays, which leaves the IPL — expected to start in March — as the next realistic window.

What it means for India and Mumbai Indians

Pandya's absence removes India's main fast-bowling all-rounder, the player who balances the side by batting in the top six and bowling a full quota of overs. India have had to look at other seam-bowling all-rounder options across the series he has missed this year, and the BCCI had reportedly hoped to manage him towards the 2027 ODI World Cup, a plan his slow recovery now complicates. For Mumbai Indians, whom Pandya captains, a return at IPL 2027 would mean their captain goes into the tournament without competitive cricket for close to ten months.

For Indian fans in the United States and elsewhere in the diaspora who follow the national team through its packed white-ball calendar, the update means at least two more series — New Zealand, then Sri Lanka and Zimbabwe — without one of the side's most recognisable players.

What's next

The next checkpoint is the start of jogging in about three weeks, followed by the eight-week running build-up. The reports stress that no return date has been fixed and that clearance will depend on how Pandya responds at each stage of rehabilitation. If the process slips further, even an IPL 2027 return would depend on a late medical clearance rather than a planned comeback date.
